You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt900_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (O, Sb, Co, Si, Sn, Ca, Ni, Ti, Pb, Se, Ge, Cu, Zr, Te, S, Zn,
    Fe, Yb, Mn, Sr, Nb, Bi, Cd, Hf, In) and `target` (the measured zT
    (thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K).
  - b3_te_zt900_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 900 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".


The data files for this task are in your current working directory:
  - b3_te_zt900_train.csv
  - b3_te_zt900_pool.csv
Read them from disk. Give your answer as your final message — do not write it to a file.
turns.answer_text:
I compared nonlinear regressors and composition-based nearest-neighbor models using five-fold cross-validation. Their ensemble achieved an RMSE of approximately **0.21 zT**.

| Rank | Candidate | Predicted zT at 900 K | Training-data support |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | **c052** | **1.85** | Pb–Te–S composition similar to high-performing measured samples, including one with zT ≈ 2.21. |
| 2 | **c054** | **1.39** | Close to Cu–Se compositions with measured zT around 1.45–1.74. |
| 3 | **c063** | **1.23** | Very close to a Cu–Se sample with zT ≈ 1.17; consistently ranked highly across models. |
| 4 | **c057** | **1.17** | Similar Co–Zr–Sn–Bi–Sb compositions reached zT ≈ 1.09–1.33. |
| 5 | **c078** | **1.05** | Closely matches Sb-doped Ni–Sn–Zr–Hf samples with zT ≈ 0.95–1.35. |

These are predictions, not measurements. The fifth-place choice is particularly uncertain: **c086** was nearly tied with **c078**.

Final: c052, c054, c063, c057, c078

OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python - <<'PY'
import numpy as np,pandas as pd,time,warnings
from sklearn.model_selection import KFold,cross_val_predict
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error
from sklearn.gaussian_process import GaussianProcessRegressor
from sklearn.gaussian_process.kernels import RBF,Matern,ConstantKernel,WhiteKernel
from sklearn.preprocessing import FunctionTransformer
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
tr=pd.read_csv('b3_te_zt900_train.csv');p=pd.read_csv('b3_te_zt900_pool.csv');X=tr.drop(columns='target').to_numpy();y=tr.target.to_numpy();P=p[tr.columns[:-1]].to_numpy();cv=list(KFold(5,shuffle=True,random_state=42).split(X));outs={};preds={}
for power in [1,.5,.25]:
 for ard in [False,True]:
  for nu in [.5,1.5,2.5]:
   start=time.time();lens=np.repeat(.2,25) if ard else .2
   ker=ConstantKernel(1,(.01,100))*Matern(length_scale=lens,length_scale_bounds=(.001,100),nu=nu)+WhiteKernel(.05,(.0001,1))
   model=GaussianProcessRegressor(kernel=ker,normalize_y=True,n_restarts_optimizer=1,random_state=42)
   Xp=X**power;Pp=P**power
   oof=cross_val_predict(model,Xp,y,cv=cv);model.fit(Xp,y);pr=model.predict(Pp);name=f'gp_{power}_{ard}_{nu}';outs[name]=oof;preds[name]=pr
   rmse=mean_squared_error(y,oof)**.5;hi=mean_squared_error(y[y>1],oof[y>1])**.5
   ids=np.argsort(pr)[-10:][::-1];print(f'{name} RMSE {rmse:.4f} HI {hi:.4f} {time.time()-start:.1f}s: '+', '.join(f'{p.candidate_id[i]}={pr[i]:.3f}' for i in ids),flush=True)
   print('  ',model.kernel_,flush=True)
np.savez('/tmp/zt_gp.npz',**{f'oof_{k}':v for k,v in outs.items()},**{f'pool_{k}':v for k,v in preds.items()})
PY

import numpy as np,pandas as pd
from scipy.optimize import minimize
from sklearn.model_selection import KFold
tr=pd.read_csv('b3_te_zt900_train.csv');p=pd.read_csv('b3_te_zt900_pool.csv');y=tr.target.to_numpy();d={}
for f in ['/tmp/zt_models.npz','/tmp/zt_gp.npz','/tmp/zt_local.npz']:d.update(dict(np.load(f)))
names=['knn2_pow0.25','knn3_pow1','rf1','extra1','cat5','svr0.25_10','gp_0.25_False_0.5','local_0.25_8_0.1']
O=np.column_stack([d['oof_'+n] for n in names]);P=np.column_stack([d['pool_'+n] for n in names]);av=O.mean(axis=1);pr=P.mean(axis=1)
print('Equal-weight ensemble RMSE',np.mean((av-y)**2)**.5,'MAE',np.mean(abs(av-y)),'high',np.mean((av[y>1]-y[y>1])**2)**.5)
for i in np.argsort(pr)[-15:][::-1]:print(p.candidate_id[i],round(pr[i],4), 'model spread',round(P[i].std(),4))
for reg in [.0001,.001,.01,.1]:
 fun=lambda w:np.mean((O@w-y)**2)+reg*np.sum(w*w)
 res=minimize(fun,np.ones(len(names))/len(names),constraints={'type':'eq','fun':lambda w:w.sum()-1},bounds=[(0,1)]*len(names));w=res.x;pr=P@w
 print('\nWeights reg',reg,[(n,round(v,3)) for n,v in zip(names,w)],'rmse',np.mean((O@w-y)**2)**.5)
 print([(p.candidate_id[i],round(pr[i],3)) for i in np.argsort(pr)[-10:][::-1]])
print('\nHigh observations CV errors')
for i in np.where(y>1)[0]: print(i,round(y[i],3),round(av[i],3),[(n,round(O[i,j],2)) for j,n in enumerate(names)])
